meta.description: Inter-regional corridor electrical parameters for DC power flow, derived from nodal/transmission_lines.geojson. Line LENGTH is computed from the geometry; REACTANCE is assigned from voltage class using standard overhead-line values (the method PyPSA and PyPSA-Eur use), then converted to per-unit on a 100 MVA base. Parallel lines on a corridor add susceptance.
meta.series_compensation: Eskom has series-compensated its 400 and 765 kV lines since 1975 (six capacitors at four sites on the Cape Corridor alone, 450-1300 Mvar). A series capacitor cancels part of the line reactance, making a compensated line electrically SHORTER. Applied here as 50% on 765 kV and 40% on 400 kV lines over 200 km. Threshold sensitivity tested across 150-300 km: corridor susceptance moves 0-16%, most under 10%. Eskom does not publish per-line compensation, so this is a heuristic; none on shorter lines. Degrees are the standard published range, NOT per-scheme Eskom settings, which are not public.
meta.hvdc_excluded: The 533 kV Apollo-Cahora Bassa circuits are HVDC and are NOT in this model. HVDC flow is set by converter controls, not by impedance, so including it in a PTDF would create loop flow through a link that cannot carry any. It is represented elsewhere as a fixed import.
meta.caveat: Reactance is ASSIGNED from voltage class, not measured. Conductor bundling, circuit count per tower and series compensation are not represented. Good enough to show that flows follow physics rather than economics; not a substitute for a real load-flow study.
